Commentary.Commentary: India go 1-0 up - So that brings us to the close of the first of the three T20Is. India have dominated this one quite comprehensively. England will go back to the drawing board to assess where things went so wrong for them. The caravan now moves to Bristol for the second T20I. That game will be played on Saturday, 30th May, with the first ball scheduled to be bowled at 7 pm IST (1.30 pm GMT). But as usual, our buildup starts well in advance. So do join us for that as well. Until then, it's goodbye. Take care, cheers!

The victorious captain of India Women - Smriti Mandhana, on the early wickets, says losing two wickets in the first over was far from ideal, especially with the Powerplay being one of India’s strengths. She credits Yastika Bhatia for shifting the momentum after returning from an eight-month break, while also praising Jemimah Rodrigues for playing her natural game. She adds that India probably left 10 runs out there but was happy with the team’s bowling and fielding effort. Speaking about the bowling plans, she says fielding second helped the side understand the conditions better, with inputs from Yastika and Jemimah proving useful. She feels the bowlers executed around 80 percent of their plans well, particularly with the way they responded after boundaries. On debutant Nandni Sharma, the skipper calls her a fiery character and praises the confidence she showed despite going for runs early on. She ends by saying that the team had already seen her quality in the WPL with Delhi Capitals, and it was impressive to watch her bounce back strongly on debut.

The captain of England Women - Charlie Dean says the two wickets were great upfront, but admits that India kept scoring runs regardless. She acknowledges that Jemimah and Yastika put on a brilliant show and admits that England failed to break the partnership early enough. With wickets in hand, she adds, India finished the innings really well, calling it a disappointing show with the bat, where they just faltered away in the end. On the bowling performance in the second half of the first innings, she says the girls put in a really good show in hot conditions and they did bounce back well. She points to real elements of positivity and says the energy in the field was great, adding that it was disappointing not to get over the line. On allowing too many runs after a bright start, she draws a parallel with Canterbury, noting that England faced a similar situation there. She highlights that they bounced back well against New Zealand and are disappointed to find themselves in the same position again. She details that England need to learn how to break momentum and swing things back in their favour. About the positives from the game, she is full of praise for the debutant Tilly Corteen-Coleman, saying she loves the way Tilly goes about her business. She is equally complimentary about Jones, saying she asked her to play a different role and she did a fabulous job. When asked whether the side is missing the experience of Nat Sciver-Brunt, she admits the big partnership was one they simply could not break with the ball. She also admits that England failed to stitch enough partnerships of their own with the bat, which would have made the chase more interesting. She says they are working on their younger middle order and have full faith they will come through.

A chaotic first innings - It took one over to flip the momentum completely. Issy Wong sprayed it everywhere in her first, leaking 27 runs and handing India the foothold they needed after losing both openers in the first over. Yastika and Rodrigues seized the moment, putting on 126 together and refusing to let England back in. Yastika's fifty announced her return to the side on a strong note, and Rodrigues was simply brutal, scoring a fluent 69 off 40 balls. England clawed back with a few wickets to raise hopes of a tighter finish, but Deepti's breezy cameo and 27 runs coming in the final two overs ensured India walked away with a total that put them firmly in control. England's fielding critically came under the scanner and they also bowled as many as 21 extras that further piled misery on them.

Perfect execution by the bowlers - The spinners found enough on the surface to extract decent purchase, and this was never a pitch that invited big shots from the off for the new batters. Dot balls accumulated, pressure mounted, and even the well-settled Amy Jones could not escape it, falling for 67. What followed was a collapse that England simply had no answer to. From 120/3, they eventually crumbled to 150/8 in a matter of moments, with Deepti and Nandni Sharma strangling the middle and lower order between them. The pace variations were expertly deployed, and India knew exactly where to bowl.

Jones-Knight fight hard, but not enough - Just like India, England also lost both their openers inside the Powerplay. The new ball swung, but the movement dried up quickly. Jones and Knight then came together to arrest the slide, with Jones the more aggressive of the two, putting her foot down and taking the attack on. Knight's stay was a lot scratchy alongside her, but together they steadied the ship and gave England something to build from with a 64-run stand. However, Knight was fished out at the worst possible time with England slipping to 101/3. And from there, the hosts just couldn't build on any partnership of real substance.

PLAYER OF THE MATCH - For her fantastic knock of 69 (40), Jemimah Rodrigues receives the award. She says that a lot of credit goes to Yastika, as she batted with an excellent strike rate, and that partnership was crucial. She adds that their conversations in the middle revolved around understanding the situation and playing smart cricket. Mentions that England were on top at that stage, making patience and sensible shot selection extremely important. Speaking about the surface, Jemimah feels there was a bit of hold initially, with Lauren Bell getting some assistance early on. She adds that the wicket was slightly slower compared to the surfaces usually seen in England. On her batting approach in T20 cricket, Jemimah shares it is a mix of instinct and awareness. With one extra fielder inside the circle, she backs her natural game but also stresses the importance of staying smart while building an innings. Talking about fielding, Rodrigues says she thoroughly enjoys being in the action and describes her time on the field as feeling like a yo-yo session. She ends by saying that she loves fielding in the hotspot and being constantly involved in the game.

India boss it up at Chelmsford - A thoroughly professional performance by the Women in Blue across all departments. They further improve their record against England in England. The hosts were completely outplayed. Though they had their moments with the ball, with the bat, they had no answers at all and just couldn't build on meaningful partnerships after the fall of the third wicket. They badly missed the services of the likes of Sciver-Brunt and also Danni Wyatt-Hodge, but they will be a lot disappointed with the sloppiness in the ground fielding this evening. So a lot to reflect on for the hosts, and they still have a couple of games to go before the big tournament coming up.

Commentary.Commentary: Time for spin now. Sree Charani is into the attack. She replaces Kranti Gaud. England Women need 131 runs from 78 balls.
Hard length and around off, Heather Knight punches it towards extra cover. 15 runs off the over!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.6: Nandni Sharma to Heather Knight, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! This is turning out to be an expensive over! Short and well outside off. Heather Knight uses the width on offer and cuts it away between point and short third for the third boundary of the over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.5: Nandni Sharma to Heather Knight, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and on middle, Amy Jones swipes it away to deep square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.4: Nandni Sharma to Amy Jones, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Two in two! Back-of-the-hand slower one, full and outside off. Amy Jones drags her sweep from there and nails it to the right of long on for another boundary. 50 up for England Women.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.3: Nandni Sharma to Amy Jones, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Up and over! Fuller delivery, on middle, Amy Jones backs away to get under it and lofts it wide of long off for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.2: Nandni Sharma to Amy Jones, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Fine effort in the deep! Short of a length and on middle, slower as well. Amy Jones waits for it and heaves it wide of deep mid-wicket. Jemimah Rodrigues quickly moves to his left and gets both her hands on the ball to parry it away. She gets up and releases the ball to keep it down to two runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.1: Nandni Sharma to Amy Jones, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: That's the end of the Powerplay. The tourists would be quite pleased to have sent both the English openers back. England need 146 runs from 84 balls. And here's Nandni Sharma (1-0-8-0) back on. She replaces Arundhati Reddy.

On a length and around off, Heather Knight steers it away towards point. There is another direct hit at the bowler's end but Jones was never in trouble. England Women are 43/2 at the end of the Powerplay.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Kranti Gaud to Heather Knight, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitched up and around off, Amy Jones drags it off the inside half of the bat to deep square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Kranti Gaud to Amy Jones, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Just short! Fuller one and on middle, Amy Jones drills it a bit aerially but on the bounce to mid on. Smriti Mandhana grabs the ball and scores a direct hit at the bowler's end, but Knight has made her ground.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Kranti Gaud to Amy Jones, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length and on off, nips back in a bit, Amy Jones stays back and pats it towards short cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Kranti Gaud to Amy Jones, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and outside off, Amy Jones punches it wide of sweeper covers for a brace.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Kranti Gaud to Amy Jones, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length and angling into the leg side, Heather Knight fails to glance it away as the ball goes off her thigh pad towards short fine. A leg bye taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Kranti Gaud to Heather Knight, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Full in length and an inswinger at the pads. Knight looks to flick but misses as the ball deflects off her pads towards backward square leg. A leg bye taken. Excellent over from Reddy. Just a couple of runs off it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Arundhati Reddy to Heather Knight, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Dishes out a good length ball around off. Knight walks down the track and defends it to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Arundhati Reddy to Heather Knight, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Wide on off, full in length. Knight leans across and eases it to the cover-point fielder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Arundhati Reddy to Heather Knight, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: An inswinger on a fuller length, Jones flicks off the pads to deep square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Arundhati Reddy to Amy Jones, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: BEATEN ALL ENDS UP! Was there an edge? Short of a good length around off, and it nips back in sharply off the surface. Jones is cut in half completely. Looks to punch it straight but the inside edge is beaten. The ball whistles over the off stump through to the keeper who fails to collect it to her left.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Arundhati Reddy to Amy Jones, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Sharp inward shape, from middle to leg, Jones tickles the full ball but straight to short fine leg.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Arundhati Reddy to Amy Jones, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Both the English openers are gone now. Heather Knight comes out to the middle.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Wicket number 2 for Kranti and Capsey is absolutely gutted. Not a wicket-taking delivery by any means, as this is too short and too wide outside off, begging to be put away. Alice Capsey presses back and looks to square cut it over point, but the ball kicks up a bit and takes a feather of the outside edge. Goes through to the keeper, where Richa Ghosh grabs it to her right very comfortably. England are 37/2, needing 152 runs.
Commentary.Howout: c Richa Ghosh b Kranti Gaud
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Kranti Gaud to Alice Capsey, OUT! c Richa Ghosh b Kranti Gaud.

Commentary.Commentary: Outside off again, short in length. Jones hangs back and cuts it to deep point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Kranti Gaud to Amy Jones, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Plays it through the gap! Short of a good length, with a lot of width on offer. Amy gets the chance to free her arms, gets on top of the bounce, and smashes it well to the left of the point fielder for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Kranti Gaud to Amy Jones, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Short and jagging back in, on middle. Alice Capsey advances a bit and pulls it to deep square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Kranti Gaud to Alice Capsey, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Absolutely crunched! Slightly short and outside off. Alice Capsey transfers her weight on the back foot and scythes it away, through point, and beats the deep backward point fielder to her right for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Kranti Gaud to Alice Capsey, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Overpitched on off, Capsey drives off the front foot to the cover-point fielder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Kranti Gaud to Alice Capsey, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A lot fuller, on the pads. Jones whips it aerially between deep square leg and deep mid-wicket for a cuple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Nandni Sharma to Amy Jones, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Wonderful shot! A half volley from Nandni, on off. Amy Jones smashes it straight down the ground and a bit uppishly. Nandni Sharma sticks her right hand out on the follow-through to pluck it, but the ball clips her fingertips and runs away to the fence for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Nandni Sharma to Amy Jones, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Touch full and nipping away from off, Amy tries to tuck it to the leg side, but closes the bat face early and a leading edge is found. The ball bounces in front of backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Nandni Sharma to Amy Jones, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A low full toss, on off, swinging away. Amy Jones takes it on the full and heaves it off the inner half. It goes on the bounce to Shafali Verma at mid on, who picks and throws in a motion to the bowling end, but misses her shy. Had the throw hit, Capsey would have been in trouble as she is forced to dive back to retreat after being sent back by her partner.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Nandni Sharma to Amy Jones, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length, shaping away gently, on top of off. Jones presses in front and blocks it down the pitch.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Nandni Sharma to Amy Jones, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and swinging away, outside off. Jones gets a good stride across and creams it to the right of the deep point fielder for a coupl of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Nandni Sharma to Amy Jones, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Nandni Sharma replaces Arundhati Reddy.
Touch full and curving in and around middle. Jones covers the line and clips it to deep backward square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Kranti Gaud to Amy Jones, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Early blow for England Women. Amy Jones walks out to bat at number 3.

OUT! MISTIMED AND GONE! Gaud strikes big and India have their first breakthrough. Hard length around the fourth stump, and Dunkley walks down the track. Flat bats it but only finds the splice. Shafali moves to her right from mid off and takes a good running catch with both hands. Dunkley was just getting started but her stay is cut short and she frustratingly walks back to the dugout. England are 18/1, chasing 189.
Commentary.Howout: c Shafali Verma b Kranti Gaud
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Kranti Gaud to Sophia Dunkley, OUT! c Shafali Verma b Kranti Gaud.

Commentary.Commentary: Way too short and outside off, Dunkley lets it be.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Kranti Gaud to Sophia Dunkley, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! That will make her feel a lot better! Fuller and around off. Sophia Dunkley collapses her back leg and it almost kisses the floor. She walks out of the crease and lofts it over mid off for a clean six.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Kranti Gaud to Sophia Dunkley, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: BEATEN! An absolute beauty from Gaud. A full ball and it straightens up the pitch, in the channel of off. Sophia Dunkley completely misses reading the line and is squared up. Tries to block from the crease, but the ball keeps leaving her and beats the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Kranti Gaud to Sophia Dunkley, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Just a hint of away shape, good length, on top of off. Capsey hangs back and punches it to deep point for a single to get off the mark.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Kranti Gaud to Alice Capsey, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Kranti Gaud to share the attack.

FOUR! Gets it away! On a good length, just outside off. Sophia Dunkley presses back and cuts it to the left of the diving backward point fielder for a boundary. 11 runs from the first over. England need 178 runs from 114 balls.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Arundhati Reddy to Sophia Dunkley, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Full and curving back onto the pads. Sophia Dunkley flicks it to the right of mid-wicket. Shafali Verma runs a bit and dives to take the sting out of the ball, parrying it to the deep for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Arundhati Reddy to Sophia Dunkley, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Swing and a miss! Full in length, outside the off pole. It lands and straightens off the pitch, beating Dunkley's desperately attempted lofted shot over the off side. The ball zips past the outside edge by a kitten-whisker.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Arundhati Reddy to Sophia Dunkley, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nice and full, around off, Dunkley strides across and taps it to point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Arundhati Reddy to Sophia Dunkley, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: EDGED AND FOUR! Oh, dear. Dunkley flirts with danger. Swings in from outside off, on a fuller length. Sophia Dunkley tries to block it away, but gets a thick inside edge and the ball just whistles past the stump, beating the keeper to her left and races to the deep fine leg fence.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Arundhati Reddy to Sophia Dunkley, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Curves down the leg stump line, on a length. Dunkley misses the flick. Wide called.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Arundhati Reddy to Sophia Dunkley, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: On the money straightaway! In-angler on a fuller length. Sophia Dunkley drops the bat down in time and carves it back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Arundhati Reddy to Sophia Dunkley, No run.
